newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba sets repo tender at unchanged fixed 3.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: Buba sets repo tender at unchanged fixed 3.00 pct.

text.p: The Bundesbank on Tuesday set a tender for 14-day securities repurchase agreements, or repos, at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.00 percent, signalling that its monetary policy stance remains unchanged for now.
Financial markets had expected the rate to remain unchanged this week but speculation that German interest rates are headed higher has mounted recently.
The market's focus is now likely to shift to Thursday, when the Bundesbank's council holds its first meeting after a four-week summer break.
A repo pact totalling 74.7 billion marks and set at a fixed rate of 3.00 percent expires on Wednesday.

Bundesbank deputy president Johann Wilhelm Gaddum gave a strong indication last week that the Bundesbank had departed from its policy of announcing terms of forthcoming weekly repo auctions after each fortnightly council meeting.
Gaddum said in a newspaper interview that the Bundesbank was operating in a "more uncertain environment" and wanted to retain full leeway each week in its repo auctions.
Many economists believe the repo rate will rise by the end of the year, more in preparation for European monetary union than to stave off domestic inflation.

But speculation of an imminent repo move in defence of the mark has been dampened by the dollar's six-pfennig fall against the mark over the last two weeks and by comments from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp who said on Monday a rate rise now would be very damaging to the domestic economy.
The dollar was quoted at 1.8320/30 marks at 0715 GMT, slightly weaker than before the repo announcement when it was quoted around 1.8360 marks.
